system_design_questions.title: URL Shortener System Design
system_design_questions.description: Design a high-scale, low-latency URL shortener service like Bitly or TinyURL. The system must support generating unique short codes, instant redirects with sub-50ms p99 latency, caching layer, and analytical click tracking.
constraints: Read to write ratio of 100:1 (4,000 reads/sec, 40 writes/sec)
URLs must be active for 5 years by default

tasks.title: Add core architectural components
tasks.description: Place API Gateway / Load Balancer, URL Service, relational database, Redis cache, and analytics worker on the canvas.

tasks.title: Connect request routing & cache-aside flow
tasks.description: Route client requests through the gateway/balancer to the URL service, and configure cache read-aside in front of PostgreSQL.

tasks.title: Model database schema & indexing
tasks.description: Define DBML schema for URLs table with unique short_code index, original_url, user_id, and click_count.

tasks.title: Define REST API contracts & architecture notes
tasks.description: Specify POST /api/v1/urls (create short link) and GET /{short_code} (redirect), and document caching trade-offs in notes.

system_design_questions.title: E-Commerce Checkout & Order Architecture
system_design_questions.description: Design an e-commerce checkout and order processing platform. The platform must prevent overselling and race conditions on high-demand flash sales, support idempotent order placements, and decouple payment processing via message queues.
constraints: Peak traffic: 50,000 concurrent checkout attempts per second during flash sales
Idempotent payment capture with third-party payment gateways

tasks.title: Decouple services with message queue & worker tiers
tasks.description: Place API Gateway, Order Service, Inventory Service, Message Queue (Kafka/RabbitMQ), and asynchronous Payment Worker.

tasks.title: Configure inventory reservation & data isolation
tasks.description: Route checkout transactions through Redis distributed locks or ACID transactional database to prevent double allocation.

tasks.title: Design schema for Orders, Order Items & Payments
tasks.description: Define DBML tables for orders, order_items, and payments with foreign keys and status tracking.

tasks.title: Define idempotent order creation API & trade-offs
tasks.description: Define POST /api/v1/orders contract with idempotency-key header, and document distributed transaction trade-offs in architecture notes.

system_design_questions.title: Ticket Booking & Seat Hold System
system_design_questions.description: Design a high-concurrency event seat reservation platform like BookMyShow or Ticketmaster. Support real-time seat availability maps, temporary 10-minute seat holds during checkout, and automatic hold expiration using TTL caching.
constraints: 100,000 users attempting to reserve seats in the first 60 seconds of ticket drop
Temporary hold lasts strictly 10 minutes before releasing back to available pool
Prevent duplicate bookings for the exact same seat across concurrent requests

tasks.title: Place core booking & seat reservation components
tasks.description: Place Client, Load Balancer, Booking Service, Redis Cache with TTL, Relational DB, and Background Expiry Worker.

tasks.title: Sequence flow for temporary seat hold & payment expiry
tasks.description: Model Mermaid sequence diagram detailing client hold request, atomic Redis seat lock, checkout redirect, and timeout release.

tasks.title: Data model for Events, Shows, Seats, and Bookings
tasks.description: Define DBML schema with seats (event_id, row, seat_number, status) and bookings with hold expiry timestamps.

tasks.title: API contracts for seat hold & reservation confirmation
tasks.description: Define GET /api/v1/events/{id}/seats and POST /api/v1/bookings/hold, and document high-concurrency consistency trade-offs.
